title: UNCERTAIN: f70v2 centre label otolal beside the star, not beside the month name 'mars'
sources: Beinecke MS 408, IIIF canvas https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/1006200 (label '70v (part)'; the Pisces wheel), region x=1600-2500, y=1200-2100 at full size: https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/1006200/1600,1200,900,900/900,/0/default.jpg

Zandbergen-Landini transliteration ZL 3b (pinned data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt), page comment for f70v2: 'In the centre are two fish ..., two stars, a word of Voynich text and the word Mars in the Roman alphabet'; the word is locus f70v2.33 under the heading 'Central star:', read otolal
Variant readings of locus f70v2.33 in the pinned transliterations: otolal (ZL 3b, RF 1b, LSI V), otylal (IT 2a, LSI H), otalal (LSI U), otral (LSI C, K); GC 2a okoeae
statement: UNCERTAIN; HERE IS WHY. I looked at the scan myself (canvas 1006200, centre cropped at full resolution). The Pisces centre holds two fish joined by a cord, two stars (one above the fish, one below), the Latin-script month name (read 'mars' in the literature; Mars = March) written between the two fish, and exactly one Voynich word. That word (otolal in ZL) is written immediately to the right of the UPPER STAR, at the top of the centre disc, the way the nymph labels on this page sit beside their stars; it is about a fish-length away from 'mars' and is not on the same line as it. ZL files it under 'Central star:'. So the scan supports reading otolal as the label of that star, and does not support it as a Voynich rendering of the month name. I file it because it is the ONLY Voynich word in any zodiac centre that I or ZL could find: I also viewed f70v1 (canvas 1006201, 'abril'), f71r (1006202, 'abril'), f73r (1006206) and f73v (1006207); each centre has the emblem and the Latin-script month name with no Voynich word beside the name; the ZL page comments for the remaining zodiac pages (f71v, f72r1-3, f72v1-3) mention no centre Voynich label either. Consequences for criterion (c): (1) the month names give no direct Voynich-word pairing; any month anchor would be an inference, not a label. (2) This pairing (otolal ~ 'mars') should NOT be confirmed on present evidence; a reviewer who agrees with my reading of the scan should file a DISSENT on the pairing so that it stays out of criterion (c). It would become usable only if a published source argues that the centre word names the month, or if the upper star is identified (a Pisces star such as the knot of the cord has been suggested in general Pisces iconography, but I found no published identification of this particular star, and I do not propose one).
